videos.title: Labour's Andy Burnham has won the Makerfield by-election. #UK #Labour #BBCNews
videos.transcript: This is the biggest bi-election I've ever covered. Why? Because one of the candidates on the ballot paper, Andy Bernham for Labour, was putting himself forward basically as a prospective prime minister. And he has won here and won big time in a place where reform did so, so well just a handful of weeks ago at the local elections. In Andy Bernham's victory speech, it was implicit, if not quite explicit, about what he would do were he to be running the country. So now what does the prime minister do? What does he say?
videos.summary: A BBC reporter covers the Makerfield by-election, where Labour's Andy Burnham won by a large margin. The reporter notes that Burnham positioned himself almost as a future prime minister during the campaign. The result raises questions about how the current prime minister will respond.

videos.title: Behind the viral praying robot bridging AI and Emirati tradition
videos.transcript: His name is Bu Sneider. We named him as a character to be close to the culture, the Emirati culture exactly. Our purpose of you know taking the Bu Sneider to greet the kids in the mosque and showing them you know how the traditional way of celebrating the Eid is [music] pure educational and we had success of that. They're understanding you know the tradition, how they greet the people, they greet the elders and all the whole ceremony you know of the Eid. Our robot is not cannot be Muslim or cannot be in a religion. It's a robot. We take it to improve our life. Robot is going to be everywhere. Not now but in a >> [music] >> decade or two kids will be grown up. So from now we want the Emirati kids, we want the people [music] of the UAE to be close to the robots.
videos.summary: The video introduces Bu Sneider, a robot designed to connect Emirati children with their cultural traditions. The robot visits mosques to demonstrate how people greet each other and celebrate Eid. Its creators hope that by introducing robots early, the people of the UAE will become comfortable with technology in the future.

videos.title: 'Absolutely freezing' winter storm causes mass power outages in US. #Storm #Weather #BBCNews
videos.transcript: Well, there are not many people out and about as you can imagine this morning. Most people are hunkering down because this is an absolutely massive storm stretching some 1500 miles across the United States. Here in Washington DC, we're expecting up to a foot of snowfall today. But in other places, southern states for example, people are just having to hang tight. Power has been knocked out. In some states, some people are without ways to heat their homes right now. Other people, they're trying to find some fun where they can. They're out sledging. A few impromptu snowball fights springing up. But certainly, people are just hanging tight because we're expecting some record snowfall. And it's not just the snow. I've got to tell you, it is absolutely freezing here. And that really gets your bonus.
videos.summary: A reporter in Washington DC describes a massive winter storm stretching 1,500 miles across the United States. The storm has caused power outages in some states, leaving people without heating, while others are making the most of the snow by sledging and having snowball fights. Record snowfall and extremely cold temperatures are expected.

options: Up to a foot of snow

multipleChoice.question: How far does the storm stretch across the United States?

options: They have no way to heat their homes
Their cars have been buried in snow

videos.title: BTS reunion set to make $1bn as band announce world tour. #BTS #KPop #BBCNews
videos.transcript: K-pop group BTS have announced a 79-day world tour and their reunion is expected to make a billion dollars. The band hasn't performed together for four years because the seven members have been completing their mandatory military service in South Korea with the last one, Sugar, finishing last June. The tour, which begins in April, will start in South Korea before setting off across Asia, Europe, and America. According to Billboard, the group and their record label stand to make more than a billion dollars. That's £740 million from their reunion from the concerts, merchandise, licensing, album sales, and streaming revenue. Their previous tour set records for a K-pop act, earning about $246 million at the global box
videos.summary: K-pop group BTS has announced a 79-day world tour after a four-year break during which all seven members completed mandatory military service in South Korea. The reunion tour is expected to generate over one billion dollars through concerts, merchandise, album sales, and other revenue streams. This would far surpass their previous record-breaking tour, which earned around $246 million.
